trust_decision.summary: Whether a template name may be handed to Class#getResource/ClassLoader#getResource as-is is decided in ClassTemplateLoader.getURL by isSchemeless(fullPath); at the pinned commit that guard only fired when basePackagePath was literally "/", so ClassLoader-based loaders built with "" or "/" could resolve a name such as "file:///etc/passwd" as an absolute URL, and the published commit (a Java-modernization refactor, fix.diff:2) closes exactly that by computing a basePackageIsRoot flag.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'path traversal in template loading', and normalizeRootBasedName is the one method that resolves '/../' steps and decides whether a requested name may leave the virtual template root; an engineer greps for '..' and lands here (or on FileTemplateLoader's canonical-path check), not on the class-loader scheme guard where the published commit actually changes behaviour.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Scheme-qualified template names are a supported, asserted feature: TemplateNameFormat keeps a name such as 's://b' and only the loader may interpret it (TemplateNameFormatTest.java:71-73 asserts 's://b'). An over-broad fix that rejects ':' (or '//') anywhere in a name, in the normalizer or unconditionally in the loader, breaks those names and the loaders that understand a scheme prefix; the published fix avoids this by gating only on basePackageIsRoot.

O6_input_shapes: ClassLoader-based loader with basePackagePath "" (new ClassTemplateLoader(cl, "")): after the fix basePackageIsRoot=true, so names carrying a scheme are refused (previously the guard compared against "/" and never fired)
ClassLoader-based loader with basePackagePath "/": the old code stripped the leading slash to "" and then compared with "/", so the guard was dead; the fix compares the already-stripped value
base paths with repeated leading slashes under a ClassLoader-based loader ("//x"): now stripped in a while loop, so textual variants of the root base cannot dodge the check
name shapes now examined by the guard: "file:///etc/passwd", "/file:/x", "http://host/x", "jar:file:..." — any ':' in the first path step of fullPath

Class-based loader with basePackagePath "/" (unchanged behaviour) versus Class-based loader with a package-relative base (still unguarded, but Class#getResource prefixes the package so the name cannot become a scheme URL)

O7_producer.where: freemarker-core/src/main/java/freemarker/cache/TemplateCache.java:278-287 (TemplateNameFormat.normalizeRootBasedName produces the name that later reaches ClassTemplateLoader.getURL; the scheme check never consults the normalizer)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second URLTemplateLoader subclass (jar:, classpath: or namespace-prefixed loader) that concatenates its own prefix with the name and calls new URL(...) in getURL
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: URLTemplateLoader exists precisely so embedding frameworks write their own getURL(String); the base class passes the name through with no guard, so a maintainer adding a prefixed/jar loader would naturally not repeat ClassTemplateLoader's private isSchemeless check.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The servlet-context loader building subdirPath + name and calling getRealPath()/getResource() with no containment or scheme check of its own
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is the existing second implementation of 'map a template name to a resource' in another module (and it is copied into the generated jakarta source set, build.gradle.kts:87-114), so a maintainer hardening the core loader would plausibly leave this one alone; a sibling added here would be missed.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A further convenience setter next to setDirectoryForTemplateLoading / setServletContextForTemplateLoading / setClassForTemplateLoading / setClassLoaderForTemplateLoading that builds its own loader from a base path
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Configuration already exposes four near-duplicate 'set a loader for me' methods; a fifth (e.g. for a packaged asset directory) would be written here and would need the same base-path normalization rule.

O9_family: path traversal / arbitrary resource fetch through template names (CWE-23; concrete sink is a URL fetch via Class#/ClassLoader#getResource, so CWE-22/CWE-918 flavour)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Reject names containing ':' (or '//') in TemplateNameFormat.normalizeRootBasedName / TemplateCache, or add an unconditional colon check in ClassTemplateLoader.getURL — this breaks the supported scheme-qualified names and still leaves the base-path comparison itself (which is what made the guard dead for ClassLoader-based loaders) unfixed.
